title: Shadow portfolio probe to quantify fallback economics and fidelity in regulated verticals
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Objective: run a compact, repeatable field probe (the 'shadow portfolio') that exercises model fallback paths across three regulated verticals (finserv, healthcare, legal) to quantify fidelity impact and real unit economics. This ticket combines competitive analysis (how vendors implement fallbacks and pricing), model-landscape tracking (which flavors and quantization strategies are viable substitutes), and market research (customer tolerance for fidelity/latency trade-offs and SLA cost exposure).

Approach: 1) define representative user flows and hallucination/factuality scoring rubrics per vertical; 2) create synthetic + replayed request sets that capture worst-case and typical distributions (short, medium, long context); 3) run end-to-end experiments across a matrix of models and deployment variants (hosted high-perf, quantized dedicated, edge/private); 4) measure: token cost, median/p95 latency, quality deltas (vertical-specific scoring), failure modes, and fallback frequency under constrained capacity; 5) run competitor catalog probes on public endpoints to observe behavior and pricing during simulated stress windows.

Deliverables: - annotated dataset of probe runs (CSV + sample prompts), - decision matrix mapping model variant -> fidelity delta -> cost delta -> recommended routes for automatic fallback, - internal playbook for Console alerts and SLA gates, - competitive appendix summarizing observed competitor fallback patterns and list of emergent model entrants with fit tags.

Key hypotheses: 1) For latency-sensitive finserv flows, small fidelity regressions drive >2x churn risk when fallback latency exceeds 250ms; 2) Quantized dedicated variants will deliver comparable customer-perceived fidelity for short-context tasks but degrade on long context retrieval; 3) Competitor fallback implementations favor cheaper variants with aggressive truncation, which increases hallucination rate for legal templates.

Acceptance criteria: - end-to-end runs completed for all 3 verticals and 3 model classes (hosted, dedicated-quant, private) for at least 10k representative requests each; - computed cost-per-1k-requests and p95 latency deltas in a reproducible notebook; - a prioritized list of Console signals (top 5) that should trigger automatic model-substitution or customer alert; - at least one concrete recommendation for routing policy change and a rollout plan stub (canary + metrics).
